program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s target binding is ambiguous and appears inconsistent with the images: the source shows a small square DVD case near the center, while the edited image shows two circular discs, one white near center-left and another white near center-right. The traces repeatedly call the center-right disc the DVD and report complete, but do not establish which edited object corresponds to the source DVD/case; the aggregate “yes” therefore conflicts with the reference “no” without identifying the visual failure. Tighten the binding to the source object using its location/appearance and require comparison with that same object in the edited image, rather than accepting any white disc as the target. Make the criterion explicitly distinguish complete, partial, absent, and unresolved based on visible evidence of the bound object’s color change; if correspondence cannot be established, return unknown rather than infer completion. Investigate the apparent extra disc/object and the source-to-edit correspondence, but do not treat repeated high-confidence traces as proof or force a “no” solely to match the reference. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
